title: Cortés, Malinche and the march to Tenochtitlan, 1519–21
summary: Cortés sailed from Cuba in February 1519 with eleven ships. He landed at Cozumel and at Tabasco, where he was given Malinche, and founded Veracruz, where he scuttled his ships. He marched inland with the Totonac and Tlaxcalans, whose help was decisive, to Tenochtitlan on 8 November. The Spanish and their allies were driven out on the Noche Triste, and took the city in August 1521 after a siege in which disease killed many.

events.label: Potonchán: Malinche given to Cortés
events.text: After the battle of Centla, the local leaders gave Cortés twenty women, among them the young woman the Spaniards baptised Marina. She spoke Nahuatl as well as Maya, and with Jerónimo de Aguilar, a Spaniard who had learned Maya, she gave Cortés a voice with the Mexica.

events.label: Tenochtitlan: Moctezuma receives Cortés
events.source: Spanish conquest of the Aztec Empire (Wikipedia)
events.text: The Mexica capital, on an island in Lake Texcoco, was larger than any city in Spain. Moctezuma received the Spanish with ceremony and lodged them in his father's palace; within a week he was a hostage.

events.label: Tenochtitlan falls
events.source: Spanish conquest of the Aztec Empire (Wikipedia)
events.text: After a siege of about eighty days Cuauhtémoc, the last tlatoani, was taken. Thousands of Tlaxcalan, Texcocan and other allies fought beside the Spanish; smallpox had reached the city in 1520 and killed a large part of its people.
